name: Echo Bat — Night Harvest
statusNote: Shipped and live; split into its own repo from star-charter on 2026-06-23. Design intent lives in the README and code comments — the SPEC doc is an unfilled template.
oneLiner: A sonar-in-the-dark game — a bat navigates a cavern by echolocation, collecting fruit and dodging pillars and owls; the world only exists where sound has touched it.
stack: single-file HTML/CSS/JS (~1390 lines), no build step

components.name: Sonar mechanic
components.desc: An auto-emitting pulse timer spawns expanding rings tested against geometry each frame; hits light up and fade, plus an always-on passive nightsight radius.

components.name: Flight physics
components.desc: Arrive-based acceleration toward the target, ambient gravity that grows when not steering, soft walls, drag, speed cap.

components.name: Level generation
components.desc: genLevel() — jagged pillar spikes, drifting spores, owls gated from level 4+, level-scaled fruit quota.

components.name: Fruit system
components.desc: Berry, plum (sings a free pulse), moth, heart.

components.name: Upgrades
components.desc: Eight tiered upgrades: Far Cry, Quick Chirp, Long Echo, Wide Band, Spare Heart, Down Feathers, Swift Wings, Nectar Sense.

components.name: Audio
components.desc: chirp() per pulse plus pickup/hit/death cues, all synthesized.

components.name: Input
components.desc: Touch, mouse, keys, and a demo-AI autopilot on the title screen.

dataFlow: Input (touch, mouse, keys, or demo-AI) sets a target position.
update(dt) applies arrive-based acceleration plus ambient gravity and drag, then integrates position with soft-wall forces.
The passive pulse timer counts down and spawns a new ring on expiry.
Active rings are tested against pillar and spore distances each frame to toggle lit state; lit state decays over time.
Fruit-proximity checks award score, healing, or pulse refresh; collisions cost HP.
draw() renders only what is lit or in passive nightsight, plus UI chrome.
Audio.chirp() fires on every pulse; other cues on pickup, hit, and death.
integrations: Shares the visual language of its siblings; no runtime dependency on star-charter or star-charter-pro
decisions: The whole design is built around geometry only existing where sound has touched it — the echo plum's free pulse reinforces the theme.
Passive nightsight gives baseline visibility so the blackout mechanic isn't punishingly opaque.
Rest-and-you-sink ambient gravity discourages passive play.
Owls are level-gated to 4+ so players learn the core mechanic hazard-free first.
Single file, zero dependencies is a locked decision — module-splitting deferred until it hurts.
